title: Queenslander exterior repaint, Trinity Beach 4879
body:
We sanded back and repainted a high-set Queenslander in Trinity Beach. The house was brown originally — the owners wanted it gone. We stripped the old finish, prepped the timber, and went with a clean coastal blue.

The tricky bit was the sand. Trinity Beach cops it from the beach, and standard exterior paint doesn't hold up. We used a sand-resistant coating designed for coastal exposure — stops the grit embedding in the finish and wearing through the top coat. Took an extra day to apply properly, but it'll add years to the repaint.

Queenslanders are all over Cairns, and Trinity Beach has a fair few. The high-set ones need proper prep on the stumps and subfloor timber — salt air gets under there and softens everything if you don't seal it right. We did the lot: boards, battens, posts, and all the trim. House looks sharp now, and the blue suits the street.

If you've got a Queenslander in Trinity Beach that's looking tired or you're sick of repainting every few years, the right prep and coating makes a difference. We've done plenty up here.

title: Queenslander exterior repaint, Trinity Beach 4879
body:
We stripped back a high-set Queenslander in Trinity Beach that'd been blue for years and took it to green. Full sand-back on all surfaces before we touched a brush — salt air up here doesn't let you skip that step.

Once the timber was clean, we applied a proper anti-corrosion coating designed for beachfront properties. It's not optional in Trinity Beach — the salt gets into everything if you don't seal it right. Then we rolled out the new colour across the weatherboards, fascias, and all the trim. Queenslanders need extra attention around the underside and the posts, so we made sure everything got covered.

Trinity Beach homes — especially the older timber ones — cop it from both ends. The wet season softens the timber, the dry season bakes it, and the salt never stops. Most exteriors up here need a full repaint every 5 to 7 years if you want to keep the house tight. This one's sorted for the next stretch.

title: Exterior repaint, black to grey, Trinity Beach 4879
body:
Full exterior repaint in Trinity Beach — previous colour was black, we've gone grey. Started with a full sand-down of the exterior, then applied a pre-paint coat to lock in adhesion. Two coats of finish paint followed. Because the house is close to the beach, we used a salt-resistant coastal protection system over the top. That extra layer keeps moisture and salt out, which matters when you're a few hundred metres from the water.

Trinity Beach homes cop it from both ends — wet season rain and year-round salt spray. Rendered brick and timber exteriors tend to fade fast without the right prep and protection. We see a lot of repaints here, usually every five to seven years, and the ones that last are the ones where the prep wasn't rushed. This one's sealed tight and should hold up well through the next few wet seasons.
